T h is appeal coming on for orders this day, t h e cou rt passed the following:
ORDER This appeal is filed by the appellant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act against an award dated 31/1/2013 passed by learned Fourth MACT, Morena in claim case No. 597/2009.

By the impugned award, the Claims Tribunal has awarded a total sum of Rs. 1,48,000/-; however, after deducting 25% towards contributory negligence, a sum of Rs. 1,11,000/- alongwith interest at the Bharat Singh vs Govind Singh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21703368/
1 rate of 7% to the appellant by way of compensation for the injuries sustained in the accident occurred on 31/1/2009.
Appellant had preferred a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.22,75,000/-.
According to the appellant compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager and deserves enhancement; however, by filing the appeal inadequacy of the compensation has been assailed.

Appellant has further assailed the deduction of 25% of award amount on the basis of contributory negligence and further assailed the impugned award on the ground of liability of payment as affixed upon respondents No. 1and 2 and exoneration of Insurance Company from payment of compensation amount.
As per the story, on the fateful day of incident i.e. 31/1/2009 the offending vehicle, a Matador was insured with appellant No. 3 Insurance Company.
Respondents No. 1 and 2, owner and driver of the offending vehicle remained ex-parte before the Claims Tribunal and so also before this Court also.
On 31/1/2009 it is alleged that appellant alongwith one Pramod Singh and Bijendra Singh were going on motorcycle to village Chamargava.
Appellant was sitting on the motorcycle in the capacity of pillion rider.

As soon as they reach in the territorial jurisdiction of Police Station Kailaras, by driving the matador in question rashly and negligently, respondent No. 2 dashed the motorcycle due to which appellant suffered grievous hurts in head, nose, face, jaws and ribs.
In respect of said accident, offence was registered vide crime No. 31/2009.
and claim petition was moved.

It is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that Claims Tribunal has found the negligence of appellant and the offending vehicle both and both were held responsible for the accident to the extent of 25x75% and accordingly the payment of compensation is to be made.

Such findings have been assailed on the insistence of the appellant in this appeal on the ground that appellant was pillion rider on the motor cycle and therefore Claims Tribunal erred in deducting 25%
of award amount towards contributory negligence.

In support of submission, she relied upon decision of Full Bench of this Court in the matter of Devisingh Vs. Vikramsingh & Ors., 2008 ACJ 393 in which it has been held that "if the damage in the accident has not been cause partly on account of violation of Section 128 of the Act by the pillion rider of the motor cycle, the pillion rider is not guilty of contributory negligence.

Similarly, if the damage suffered by the pillion rider has not been caused partly on account of violation of Section 128 of the Act by the driver, the pillion rider cannot put up a plea of composite negligence by the driver.

In other words, if breach of Section 128 of the Act, does not have a causal connection with the damage caused to the pillion rider, such breach would not amount to contributory negligence on the part of the pillion rider of the motor cycle or composite negligence on the part of the driver of the motor cycle."
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that on account of accident the appellant has suffered the permanent disability/grievous injuries due to fracture sustained.
It is also submitted that on account of injuries the injured could not perform the work during treatment and also not in a position to work properly in future.

Counsel further submits that the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is inadequate, without looking to the injuries sustained, permanent disability,
hospitalization, medical bills etc. and the future loss of earning, however it is liable to be enhanced.

Bharat Singh vs Govind Singh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21703368/
2

Learned counsel appearing for the respondent Insurance Company has relied upon the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal and further argued that the compensation awarded is just, proper and reasonable Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

After having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and looking to the permanent disability/grievous injuries sustained by the injured and after taking into consideration, the hospitalization and medical bills and also the future loss of earning, it appears that the amount awarded by the learned Tribunal is on lower side and deserves enhancement.
Thus, looking to all the facts and evidence available on record, I am of the considered opinion that the Award passed by the Claims Tribunal deserves to be enhanced by Rs.40,000/-.

As regards contributory negligence as fixed by the Claims Tribunal, in the light of decision of Apex Court in the matter of Devisingh (supra), here in the present case, it is not in dispute that breach of Section 128 of the Act, does not have a causal connection with the damage caused to the pillion rider.
Thus, the finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal regarding deduction of compensation amount to the extent of 25% towards contributory negligence is hereby set aside.

As regards question of shifting of liability over the Insurance Company is concerned, while passing the impugned award,learned Claim Tribunal shifted the burden of payment of impugned award over respondents No. 1 and 2 while exonerating Insurance Company on the ground that on the date of incident, respondent No. 2-Driver was not having valid and effective driving licence for driving transport vehicle as he was having LMV licence.

The aforesaid controversy has been put to rest by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra) while holding that "a person holding driving licence to drive 'light motor vehicle'
is competent to drive transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7,500 kgs or a motor car, tractor or road-roller, the unladen weight of which does not exceed 7.500 kgs."
Undisputedly, the respondent No. 2 was holding a LMV licence at the time of incident and was driving a transport vehicle, whose unladen vehicle weight in the instance case as per submission of parties is below 7,500 kgs and therefore, in light of aforesaid decision the finding given by Claims Tribunal regarding liability of payment of compensation amount is set aside and Insurance Company is held liable for payment of compensation amount instead of respondents No. 1 and 2.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this appeal is allowed in part and the appellant is held entitled to receive enhanced compensation of Rs.40,000/- in addition to the amount of compensation of Rs.
1,48,000/- already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till its realization.
The Insurance Company shall make the payment of compensation amount to the appellant within two months from today.
In the facts and circumstances of the case parties are directed to bear their own costs.
Appeal stands allowed in part and disposed of.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
